title: Identification and Estimation of Intergenerational Income Mobility Measures
abstract: arXiv:2609.04994v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Measuring the intergenerational transmission of lifetime economic status is complicated by researchers often only observing snapshots of income at specific ages. Consequently, standard practice estimates intergenerational mobility using income averages, introducing life-cycle bias that compromises reliability and comparability across studies, time, and place. I develop a missing data framework that exploits available income data and observable characteristics to eliminate life-cycle bias. This method combines nonparametric identification with Neyman-orthogonal moments to construct debiased machine learning estimators for intergenerational income mobility measures under plausible missing-at-random and testable independence assumptions. I apply this framework to estimate the intergenerational elasticity for the U.S. using the Panel Study of Income Dynamics across birth cohorts from 1954 to 1977 with rolling 10-year windows. translated_title: 代际收入流动性测度的识别与估计
translated_abstract: 衡量终身经济地位的代际传递因研究者通常只能观察到特定年龄的收入“快照”而变得复杂。因此，标准做法是使用收入平均值来估计代际流动性，但这会引入生命周期偏差，损害了研究结果在不同研究、时间和地点之间的可靠性与可比性。我开发了一个缺失数据框架，利用可获得的收入数据和可观察特征来消除生命周期偏差。该方法将非参数识别与Neyman正交矩相结合，在合理的随机缺失假设和可检验的独立性假设下，构建了代际收入流动性测度的去偏机器学习估计量。我将该框架应用于美国收入动态追踪研究（PSID）数据，采用滚动10年窗口，估计了1954年至1977年出生队列的代际收入弹性。而现有的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一个缺失数据框架，将非参数识别与去偏机器学习相结合，消除代际收入流动性估计中的生命周期偏差，并利用PSID数据估计了美国1954至1977年出生队列的代际收入弹性。
